Starts from S1 90° / S2 90°. Same direction adds the offset to both angles; opposite adds it to S1 and subtracts it from S2. Keys E/D.

Quick moves

Keys: Q/A S1, W/S S2 (hold Shift for 10°), R record, Space play.

In each segment both servos move from their start angle to their end angle at the same time. Segments play in order.

Easing Repeat Times
—

Record while you move the sliders or drag the S1 × S2 path, then play it back. Saving it as an Arduino case simplifies it to a handful of moves (anything within 3° is dropped).

—

Wekinator outputs a class → Processing sends that number over serial → Arduino plays the matching case. Each case is a few moveTo() lines. 0 always returns to the rest pose (the CAD pose).

Add cases from the Sequence or Record tab. Up to 9 cases (Wekinator classes 1–9).

Arduino: S1 on pin 9, S2 on pin 10, 9600 baud. Processing needs the oscP5 library and listens for /wek/outputs on port 12000.

An unloaded SG90 does about 0.1 s per 60° (≈600°/s at 4.8 V). Under load it is slower.

Default: as the angle goes up, the horn turns counter-clockwise seen from the horn side. If your horns weren't fitted at 90°, enter the real values here so the simulated angles match the numbers you pass to write().

Rods are treated as rigid: horn hole to head ear is fixed (A 39.4 mm, B 35.6 mm). Your string joints can only pull, so the real head will have some slack.

Collision check covers the head and yoke against the frame and servo bodies, from mesh point clouds. Rods and horns are not checked.
